dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Model publishes δZ_station = baseline × coverage × FSF. Baseline = 2017 Boulder single-station eclipse observation. FSF = H(r)/r station-to-station factor. Under V12 (r·tan(θ)=H(r)), FSF = H(r)/r = tan(θ) = tan(lat) — a pure trig identity on geographic latitude, H(r)-independent. Unchanged from c9; post-c10 patches align text to this pipeline description at both detail-tier fields.

kernel_of_truth.description: The FSF ratio genuinely does reproduce the observed 9-station pattern to Pearson r ≈ 0.9999 (data/wins.json:025.detail_evidence, verbatim at HEAD 2ffa5bd). The dome DID publish an equation that generates the correct station-to-station scaling. What EXP-624 proved (see data/wins.json:010 detail_evidence 5 V12 + 6 tan(lat) mentions, and data/wins.json:025 detail_evidence 1 V12 + 2 tan(lat) mentions post-ISS-2956) is that the same ratio would be generated by any smooth H(r) satisfying V12 — the ratio's H(r) dependence is algebraically inert. So the dome is 'right about the numbers' (kernel of truth) while being 'wrong about why the numbers came out that way' (H(r)-independence means the derivation is a trigonometric identity on geographic latitude, not a novel dome-geometric result).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A trigonometric identity on geographic latitude is not a scientific prediction — it is a mathematical tautology under V12. Any smooth H(r) satisfying V12 (including standard-Euclidean flat H, exponential H, polynomial H, oscillatory H) produces the same tan(lat_i)/tan(lat_BOU) ratio. The dome's specific exponential H(r) is neither necessary nor sufficient for the observed 9-station pattern — the pattern is a consequence of geographic latitude, full stop. Meanwhile the absolute magnitude (which is where a prospective test would live) is imported from the 2017 Boulder observation (data/wins.json:025.detail_evidence 'the \'baseline\' term is imported from the 2017 Boulder single-station observation'). Verdict 'Std Model Explains' correctly captures both: standard Chapman-Sq physics explains the magnitude AND the standard formula δZ ∝ f(coverage, geometry) explains the station-to-station scaling.
